html:
Another day of eating, loafing and waiting to die; another day I can’t remember doing anything in.

Woke at 6:30 and video-chatted with my wife for an hour from bed. By 7:30 it was fully light; I got up, ate, and went to the supermarket with Mom to buy things to take back with me: hazel mushrooms, wood ear fungus, fermented tofu, sunflower seeds, pine nuts, glass noodles. I also wanted some powdered milk from Feihe, the local dairy brand, but it only came in tins, which take up too much space, and was either for babies or for the middle-aged and elderly.

We chatted at home for a bit and then it was noon, time to make dumplings stuffed with pickled cabbage. After lunch Mom and I went to buy pajamas. I said I’d get her some at Zara back in Germany; she said that was too expensive. Then she bought a set for over 400 yuan, and once we got home she regretted it: too expensive. I’ve been shopping a few times since I got back, and I’ve noticed that shop assistants here are far too enthusiastic. Faces wreathed in smiles, they compliment the customer from every angle, head to toe, in endlessly inventive ways, and every single garment comes with its own unique backstory. From the moment you walk in, through the fitting room, to the checkout, you don’t get a moment’s peace. After years of Europe’s self-service shopping, being fawned over like a star every time you buy something is excruciatingly awkward.
